title: Short-form customer advisory: model fallthrough + recommended client actions (EU)
body:
Summary:

On 2028-09-13 (UTC), a subset of requests routed to our EU serving cluster experienced repeated model fallthroughs where the primary model failed to generate responses and the automated fallthrough sequence retried incompatible model variants. This produced elevated error rates and truncated responses for ~2.5% of active tenants in eu-west-1 for a 3h window (12:07–15:08 UTC).

Impact (customer-facing):
- Symptom: intermittent 5xx errors and truncated streaming sessions when hitting generation endpoints (text-generation / chat).
- Scope: approximately 2.5% of requests originating in EU regions during the window; affected tenants saw decreased throughput and occasional connection resets.
- Severity: degraded functionality for generation calls; embeddings and non-inference control-plane calls were unaffected.

What happened (plain language):
- Our smart routing logic attempted to reroute traffic from a saturated model variant to fallback variants automatically. An unexpected compatibility mismatch between a new fallback variant and our fallthrough orchestration logic caused repeated retries and an improper in-flight model swap. The retries exacerbated load on the EU pool and increased latency, leading to cascading failures for a subset of requests.

Immediate remedial actions we took (chronology):
1) 12:12 UTC: Detected elevated error rates and opened INC-9123.
2) 12:20 UTC: Disabled automated fallthrough routing to stop repeated retries across model families.
3) 12:35 UTC: Pinned live traffic to the last-known-good model variant for affected tenants in eu-west-1.
4) 13:10 UTC: Scaled additional ephemeral capacity for the EU pool to relieve queuing pressure.
5) 15:05 UTC: Began progressive re-enable of controlled fallbacks with compatibility checks; monitoring observed normal error rates by 15:08 UTC.

What this means for you and recommended short-term actions: (concise actionable steps you can take now)
- If you rely on strict latency guarantees: temporarily pin your calls to a stable model variant using the model parameter (example):

  - SDK / API snippet:
    - curl example:
      curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\\n        -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \\\n        -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\\n        -d '{"model":"rwd-gpt-7b-stable-v1","input":"<your prompt>","stream":false}'

    Replace "model" with the pinned model name above. Pinning avoids any automated fallthrough during the next 48 hours while we finish compatibility validation.

- If you use streaming: enable the client-side retry guard (idempotency token + max-retries=1) to avoid duplicate partial streams. Example header: X-Idempotency-Key: <uuid> and set max-retries=1 in your SDK config.

- If you observe truncated structured outputs: add a simple client-side post-check that re-requests the last 64 tokens when the response ends unusually (we can provide a tiny helper script on request).

Security and data concerns:
- There is no indication of customer data leakage. The incident involved service routing and model compatibility only; control plane and storage systems were not impacted.

SLA / billing note:
- We are evaluating SLA credit eligibility for affected customers; if your production traffic experienced sustained errors during the window above and you rely on a paid SLA, please open a case with billing referencing INC-9123. We will expedite the review.

Next steps (what we're doing):
- Completed: disable automated fallthrough, pin affected tenants, and add capacity to stabilize the pool.
- In progress: a compatibility validation suite for fallthrough variants (will run in pre-production on every model onboarding), expected complete 2028-09-21.
- Planned: rollout a single-step coordinated model swap API that lets tenants opt into controlled fallbacks; ETA Q4 2028.

How we'll keep you informed:
- Status page: a brief incident note has been posted and will be updated with the postmortem link once finalized.
- Direct customers: if you are on a Dedicated or Private plan and were impacted, your Customer Success rep will reach out with a tailored timeline and recommended pinning strategy.

Who to contact now:
- For urgent production impact: open an incident via the portal (link in status page) and reference INC-9123.
- For billing/SLA inquiries: support+billing@redwood.ai with subject "INC-9123 SLA review".
- For technical guidance on pinning or SDK changes: reach out to your Solutions Engineer or email cs-tech@redwood.ai.

Short closing note:
We recognize the disruption this caused and are prioritizing changes that eliminate this class of fallthrough loop while giving you explicit controls to avoid automated swaps when you need deterministic behavior. Apologies for the impact — we will follow up with a full postmortem with logs, root-cause detail, and a timeline for the compatibility test suite.

Appendix: quick FAQ (short)
Q: Will pinning increase my cost?
A: Pinning to a stable variant may change unit-cost slightly if the pinned variant has a different efficiency profile. We can provide per-tenant cost delta estimates on request.

Q: Can you roll my tenant back to pre-incident routing permanently?
A: Yes — request a routing policy change via the customer portal or ask your CS rep; this is a policy-only change and can be applied quickly.

Q: When will fallthrough automation be safe again?
A: We expect the compatibility validation suite to be runnable for all new fallbacks by 2028-09-21, after which we will re-enable automated fallthrough in a phased manner across regions.

-- End of short advisory.
